current_contexts.paragraph:
\section{Introduction}
OpenROAD and OpenLane provide open synthesis and physical-implementation
infrastructure~\cite{ajayi2019,shalan2020}. Release combines geometric,
connectivity and timing evidence bound to the selected implementation and
verification inputs. A zero-marker report may concern another GDS or omit
required rules; repair can invalidate earlier evidence.

\FloatBarrier
\section{Related Work}
OpenROAD and OpenLane provide implementation infrastructure
~\cite{ajayi2019,shalan2020}. METRICS2.1 structures flow measurement and
parameter tuning~\cite{jung2021}, and PROV represents provenance
relationships~\cite{prov2013}. Nix supports fixed-output hashing and
experimental content-addressed derivations; Bazel maps action hashes to
cached results and stores outputs by content~\cite{nixdocs,bazeldocs}.
SLSA build provenance relates artifact digests to build definitions and
builder identities~\cite{slsadocs}. These mechanisms can carry domain-specific
checks as declared actions and policies. This evaluation specializes release
acceptance to native EDA invocation, report structure, approved inputs, and
cached lineage; it does not evaluate Nix/Bazel execution or SLSA conformance.

current_contexts.paragraph:
A typed change rolls execution back to its earliest affected stage and
invalidates downstream evidence. The recorded live episodes configure three
attempts per stage and 24 diagnosis attempts. These settings do not establish
universal termination. The controller stops when a
proposal would revisit a previously failed stage fingerprint, including its
inputs and effective configuration. Formal equivalence checks both synthesis
and routed netlists using EQY~\cite{eqydocs}. Scalar-net matching uses
\code{splitnets on}; grouping related signals under \code{[collect *]} and
\code{group *} preserves coupled-state proof structure. Fresh counter and
shift-register controls prove equivalent, while a retained counter mutant
with a forced flop fails equivalence.

43(10), 3184--3197 (2024). \url{https://doi.org/10.1109/TCAD.2024.3383347}

current_contexts.paragraph:
ChatEDA studies model-driven EDA task
planning, script generation, and execution~\cite{chateda}. ORFS-agent
optimizes OpenROAD-flow-scripts parameters~\cite{orfsagent}; MCP4EDA connects
model interaction to RTL-to-GDS execution and backend synthesis feedback
~\cite{mcp4eda}. FlowFixer-EDA uses log extraction, patch validation, and
native tool feedback for diagnosis and repair~\cite{flowfixer}. Its patch
validation already demonstrates the importance of rechecking. Here, the
specific object of study is the release contract binding the selected GDS,
approved verification inputs, native report structure, and cached gate lineage.
EDAid uses
multiple model-controlled agents for EDA workflow execution~\cite{edaid}.
Ghose et al. study executable OpenROAD changes and measured quality of
results~\cite{audopeda}. The newer author conference manuscript also records
patch/snapshot/proof manifests and renewed checks. These overlap with generic
manifest-based revalidation; no priority for that mechanism is claimed.

Ghose, A., Kahng, A.B., Kundu, S., Wang, Z.:
ORFS-Agent: Tool-Using Agents for Chip Design Optimization.
In: Proceedings of the ACM/IEEE International Symposium on Machine Learning
for CAD (MLCAD), pp. 1--13 (2025). \url{https://doi.org/10.1109/MLCAD65511.2025.11189204}

current_contexts.paragraph:
ChatEDA studies model-driven EDA task
planning, script generation, and execution~\cite{chateda}. ORFS-agent
optimizes OpenROAD-flow-scripts parameters~\cite{orfsagent}; MCP4EDA connects
model interaction to RTL-to-GDS execution and backend synthesis feedback
~\cite{mcp4eda}. FlowFixer-EDA uses log extraction, patch validation, and
native tool feedback for diagnosis and repair~\cite{flowfixer}. Its patch
validation already demonstrates the importance of rechecking. Here, the
specific object of study is the release contract binding the selected GDS,
approved verification inputs, native report structure, and cached gate lineage.
EDAid uses
multiple model-controlled agents for EDA workflow execution~\cite{edaid}.
Ghose et al. study executable OpenROAD changes and measured quality of
results~\cite{audopeda}. The newer author conference manuscript also records
patch/snapshot/proof manifests and renewed checks. These overlap with generic
manifest-based revalidation; no priority for that mechanism is claimed.

current_contexts.paragraph:
ChiBench supplies RTL designs for EDA-tool testing~\cite{chibench}.
DRVerify documents physical-verification runset testing with known legal
and violating structures~\cite{drverify}. That runset-testing rationale motivates checking rule execution and intended
coverage in addition to marker counts. The
present contribution combines constructed native/ledger faults, candidate
lineage, fresh recorded-proposal checks, and artifact-level repeat evidence.
Comparable contracts in other controllers are not excluded by this study.

claim_alignment.claim_summary: Runset testing uses known legal and violating structures; zero markers alone do not prove rule intent/coverage.
claim_alignment.supported_scope: White paper describes PASS/FAIL test generation and the distinction between executable runsets and intended design rules.
limitations: This is vendor documentation, not a peer-reviewed efficacy study. SemiWiki is the host, not the author/publisher identity.
The zero-marker inference is an interpretation of the cited rationale; it is not a reported result about this study's 211-rule deck.
claim_alignment.recommended_wording: Sage's DRVerify white paper describes runset testing with passing and failing layout structures. This illustrates why rule intent and coverage require testing beyond a clean report on one layout.

recommended_corrections.action: Use Sage Design Automation, Inc., exactly as shown in the PDF.
Attribute the rule-intent/coverage inference specifically to the vendor white paper and separate it from ChiBench.
